sentences.text: Foundry is the Azure platform where teams build agents with their own code and models.
Copilot Studio can invoke one of those agents, like a boss who calls an outside specialist.
This capability is in preview.
It is a way to reuse the work of another team.
You go to Agents, Add an agent, Connect to an external agent, and choose Microsoft Foundry.
The connection needs the project endpoint.
Then you enter a name, a description, and the Agent Id.
It is only a few details, but each one matters for the connection to work.
First requirement: the agent must have the Activity protocol enabled.
New agents expose only Responses and A two A.
You can enable it only through the R E S T A P I or the Python S D K.
If it is missing, you see a four hundred error.
Knowing this saves you hours of searching.
Second requirement: only agents created in the new Foundry portal work.
With the previous portal, the error is four hundred four, Version not found.
Each error code tells a different story.
If it is four hundred four, look at where the agent was created.
If you see a four hundred four error, the agent is from the old portal.
And here is the classic trap: looking for the Activity protocol in the portal, where only Responses and A two A appear.
With this method you win easy points on a diagnosis question in the exam.
